mainEntity.name: Webflow vs WordPress — which is better for a Swiss SME in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most Swiss startups and SMEs, Webflow wins. No plugin vulnerabilities, no monthly security patches, no 'who's maintaining the server?' conversations. Webflow handles hosting, SSL, CDN, and backups natively — while giving your team a visual CMS they'll actually use. WordPress still makes sense for heavy e-commerce or complex custom apps. For marketing sites, product sites, portfolios, and lead-gen pages — Webflow is faster to ship, cheaper to maintain, and far more secure long-term.

mainEntity.name: Can I edit and update the site myself after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — that's the whole point. Webflow's CMS is designed for non-developers: edit copy, swap images, publish blog posts, update team members, launch new case studies. I structure every build with clear collections, sensible field names, and editor-only permissions so your team can ship updates without fear of breaking layouts. You also get a short Loom walkthrough covering the exact workflows for your site.

mainEntity.name: Do you integrate AI features, chatbots, or automations into Webflow sites?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — and it's one of the fastest-growing requests in 2026. Common setups include AI-powered search, OpenAI or Claude-driven chat assistants, lead-qualification bots, n8n or Make automations triggering on form submissions, and auto-generated CMS content from approved sources. Built properly — with rate limits, fallbacks, and brand-safe guardrails — so the AI layer actually helps your business instead of becoming the next thing to babysit.
